summary: The trigger list in the proposal is implemented. HostedHubSession has probe() and resume(), with a 5 s bound. The web lifecycle calls them on visibilitychange, resume, online, pageshow and NetworkInformation change. A 5 s stall watch on unary requests also calls probe(). While a probe is armed, new logical streams are held back. One scenario named in the finding still waits up to 45 s: a NAT rebinding or path change with no browser signal while the user only watches streams (an agent running) and sends no unary request. In that case the logical channel's Effect RpcClient ping timeout (16-24 s) tears the channel down, but neither that timeout nor the unintentional close calls probe(). The replacement relay stream therefore opens at once on the still-#ready dead account socket (hostedHubSession.ts:148). This is exactly the gap the original verifier flagged. Recovery waits for the 45 s session heartbeat. The fix also has a plausible regression. The probe's ping goes into the same FIFO queue as data, behind up to about 2 MiB of outbound bytes. A large unary upload on a slow uplink can trip the stall probe at about 10 s, kill the upload and repeat on every retry. Before the fix, the same upload survived until the 16-24 s RpcClient ping timeout.

evidence.note: probe() is implemented as described: 5 s deadline, reuses a pending heartbeat nonce, and fails at once when silent past the 45 s bound.
New streams are held back only while #probeDeadline is armed. With no probe armed, a replacement stream opens on the dead socket because #ready is still true.

probe or resume is called on visibilitychange, resume, online, pageshow and NetworkInformation change. All of these are browser signals that a NAT rebinding may never fire. Safari and Firefox have no navigator.connection.
The stall watch is armed only for unary requests (`if (!info.stream)`). Thread and shell streams, the main traffic while an agent runs, are never watched.
An unintentional logical-channel close calls connectionClosed and starts a reconnect, but no probe.
The hosted lifecycleHandlers set no onHeartbeatTimeout. The RpcClient ping-timeout hook exists (rpc/protocol.ts:48, 502-510) but nothing forwards it to probeHubSubscription.

The Effect pinger pings every 8 s and fires its timeout after 16 s of silence, so 16-24 s. A ping timeout fails the socket read and the retry policy reconnects. That makes a new BrowserHostedRelaySocket, then session.createSocket(), which opens on the dead account socket.
controller.connectionClosed only patches reconnecting or stale. It does not probe the account socket.

#send is FIFO for every frame type. A ping goes behind queued data, up to HUB_SESSION_MAX_QUEUED_BYTES (2 MiB) including physical bufferedAmount. The probe deadline starts at enqueue time, not when the ping leaves.
RELAY_MAX_RPC_MESSAGE_BYTES is 4 MiB. Image attachments travel inline as dataUrl in unary dispatch (orchestration.ts:599-607), so one unary request can be several MiB.
The Hub sends flow.pause/resume only on backpressure toward the consumer. A slow client uplink produces no inbound frames that could satisfy the probe during a large upload.

The tests cover probe success and failure, nonce reuse, silent-past-bound, held streams and carried pending streams. Nothing covers a probe behind a congested send queue, and no transport test covers probing on a channel close or ping timeout.

remaining: (1) A path change with no browser signal while only streams are active, the common case of watching an agent run, still takes up to 45 s. The logical channel's RpcClient ping timeout (16-24 s) and unintentional channel closes (transport.ts:515-530) do not probe. The replacement stream then opens immediately on the dead account socket (hostedHubSession.ts:148), and recovery waits for the session heartbeat (hostedHubSession.ts:468-497). (2) Fix defect: probe() starts its 5 s deadline while the ping may still sit behind up to 2 MiB of queued data (hostedHubSession.ts:202-215, 433-435). A large unary upload on a slow uplink can be misclassified as a dead socket.
fixDefects: Plausible false-positive regression. The stall watch (transport.ts:567-590) fires 5 s after a unary request starts, including while that request's own multi-MiB payload is still uploading. probe() then enqueues its ping FIFO behind up to about 2 MiB of session-queued and browser-buffered data (hostedHubSession.ts:408-436) and arms a 5 s deadline at enqueue time. If no inbound frame arrives in that window, #lost('network') closes every logical stream, marks the dispatch delivery-unknown and reconnects. No inbound frame arrives when no other stream is chatty and no Hub heartbeat lands; the Hub sends no flow frames toward a slow producer. Example: a 1.5-4 MiB image dataUrl on a 1-3 Mbps uplink. It used to succeed if the upload finished before the 16-24 s RpcClient ping timeout. Now it fails at about 10 s, and every retry fails the same way. Minor: #unansweredRequests is not cleared on an unintentional close (transport.ts:515-530), and the exit and interrupt hooks are skipped while the lifecycle is inactive. Stale entries can each fire one extra probe after a reconnect. That is harmless apart from one held RTT.
implementationSketch: A. Probe on logical-channel suspicion (packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts, lifecycleHandlers()). Add `onHeartbeatTimeout: () => { if (!this.#disposed) this.#binding.requestStalled?.(); }`. In onClose, when !context.intentional, call `this.#binding.requestStalled?.()` before connectionClosed. Optionally rename the binding hook to `connectionSuspect`. The protocol's onPingTimeout hook runs before the RpcClient retry builds the replacement socket, so the probe is armed before session.createSocket(). hostedHubSession.ts:148 then holds the new stream until a frame proves the account socket alive, or carries it to the replacement READY (PENDING_STREAM_MAX_WAIT_MS). Optional tighter version: arm a 5 s timer on onHeartbeatPing and clear it on onHeartbeatPong/onRequestChunk, so stream-only sessions are probed within about 8+5 s of path death. Only do this after B. Also clear #unansweredRequests in the unintentional-close branch. B. Make the probe congestion-aware (hostedHubSession.ts). (1) Give ping and pong control frames priority: in #send, when the queue is non-empty, unshift control frames instead of pushing. Hub-session frames are atomic and stream-independent, so a ping may overtake data. (2) Start the probe deadline only when the ping has been handed to the physical socket, i.e. in #scheduleDrain when it leaves the queue. (3) At the deadline, if no frame has arrived but `#queueBytes + socket.bufferedAmount` has shrunk since the previous check, re-arm once more. Stay bounded by HUB_SESSION_DEAD_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS since #lastReceived. Tests: in hostedHubSession.test.ts, give the fake socket bufferedAmount >= 256 KiB and queued data. Assert the ping is sent ahead of queued data, that steady drain progress keeps the session past 5 s, and that no progress loses it at 5 s. In transport.test.ts, assert that onHeartbeatTimeout and an unintentional onClose call probeHubSubscription once, and that an intentional close does not. Add an integration-style test (HostedRelaySessionIntegration or hostedHubSession plus transport): after a ping timeout, the replacement stream is not opened on the suspect socket before a frame arrives.
decisionReason: Client-only change inside the existing probe path. Failures still flow through HostedHubSession.#lost → stream closes → transport/controller, so hosted lifecycle ownership is unchanged. There is no Hub protocol change: a ping overtaking queued data frames is already legal because frames of different streams interleave. No E2EE or auth semantics are touched.
